speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To narrow down the cause of your double vision, limb weakness, and difficulty climbing stairs, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or gradually? Additionally, do you notice any trouble speaking or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is highly suggestive of Myasthenia Gravis, but we must rule out other neurological causes. REQUEST TEST: Antibody_panel_for_myasthenia_gravis (AChR, MuSK). Please also undergo a Tensilon test and an Edrophonium test during your next visit.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; Chest_CT: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The presence of elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, combined with your history of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity, confirms this diagnosis. Since your chest CT was normal, we have successfully ruled out a thymoma for now, but we will monitor for thymic abnormalities over time.
